gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: I couldn’t find anything about pushchairs in the show rules. Bicycles and scooters are banned, apart from mobility aids, and it’s all grass, so I would ask the show before you go.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: Pets aren’t allowed at the airshow, only guide dogs and assistance dogs. The aerodrome welcomes dogs on normal days, but that doesn’t apply on show weekend.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: When I last checked, the rules didn’t say whether you can bring a picnic or your own alcohol. There are more than 20 food and drink stands, so I would check the FAQ or ask the show before you pack a cool box.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: Nothing is said about chairs, windbreaks or gazebos. Ladders and step stools can be taken off you at the gate, and tripods mustn’t block anyone’s view, so I would ask before you bring anything big.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: The campsite has a fresh water point, but I couldn’t see refills listed for day visitors. I would bring plenty to drink and a refillable bottle.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: There are accessible toilets on site, but I couldn’t find a Changing Places toilet listed. The show asks you to get in touch about access needs before you visit, and I would do that.

gtk.title: Carers' tickets
gtk.text: A carer ticket costs the same as a child ticket, one per disabled visitor, booked alongside their ticket. Bring proof such as a Blue Badge in case you’re asked at the gate.

gtk.title: Hearing support
gtk.text: I couldn’t find anything about hearing loops or BSL. The show warns that the engines are extremely loud, so if anyone in your group has sensitive hearing, I would get in touch before you go.

gtk.title: Quiet area
gtk.text: There’s no quiet or sensory space listed. Your child’s ears are delicate, so try to protect them as much as possible, and think about where you could step away from the crowd line if it all gets too much.

gtk.title: Re-entry
gtk.text: You can leave and come back on the same day, as long as you keep on the wristband you’re given at the gate. Bear in mind cars may be held in the car parks while the flying is on.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: The first aid point isn’t published. Children must be with an adult at all times, so I would agree a meeting point when you arrive and tell the nearest member of staff straight away if you get separated.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm. The show goes ahead in the rain, but the flying can change at short notice, and tickets are only refunded if the whole show is cancelled.

days.html:
Pick Your Day

Saturday and Sunday run to the same times, and the 2027 line-up isn’t due until the new year. So for most people it comes down to what suits your weekend. Tickets are for the date you book and can’t be swapped, so it’s worth a minute’s thought. How about camping and doing both?

Show days26 and 27 June
Gates10:00 to 18:00
FlyingFrom about 12:00
CampingBoth days included
FridayFutures and Arrivals Day on 25 June. Watch the display aircraft arrive and rehearse. £7.50, and free for schoolchildren and veterans.
SaturdayCar parks from 09:00, gates and ground show at 10:00, flying from about 12:00 and the show closes at 18:00.
SundayThe same times as Saturday. Car parks from 09:00, gates at 10:00, flying from about 12:00, close at 18:00.
The WeekendCamp on the airfield beside the Mustang entrance, with entry on both show days for everyone on the booking. Early bird £149 for up to two, or £240 for up to four.

Are you staying over?

How far are you travelling?

Fancy seeing them arrive on Friday?

I Would Pick The Sunday

  1. WhyIf you’re local, a Sunday out at Headcorn is an easy one. You get the same times and the same ground show, without giving up your Saturday.
  2. Good to knowEveryone leaves by the same country roads when the show closes at 18:00. If you need to be home at a set time, I would leave a little before the end, or stay on and look round the traders while the rush clears.
  3. Getting thereThe car parks open at 09:00, free and first come first served. Try to arrive early if you want a front row pitch. More in .

I Would Pick The Saturday

  1. WhyIf you’re coming a long way, Saturday leaves you Sunday to get home and rest before the week starts. And if you’re at the Friday arrivals, it follows straight on.
  2. Good to knowYour ticket is only valid for the date you book, so I wouldn’t try to pick by a long range forecast. Head to the crowd line first and save your pitch, then look round the static aircraft and the traders before the flying.
  3. Getting thereRooms in the villages are limited, so I would book somewhere as soon as you have your tickets. More in .

I Would Camp For The Weekend

  1. WhyYou get both show days from the same pitch, and if the weather spoils one, you still have the other. Children love waking up to the sound of engines starting.
  2. Good to knowArrive Thursday 12:00 to 21:00, Friday 10:00 to 21:00 or Saturday 08:00 to 18:00, and leave by 12:00 on Monday. There are toilets, showers and fresh water, but no hook ups, and quiet hours are 22:30 to 07:00.
  3. Getting therePitches must be booked ahead, as there’s no camping sale on the gate. More in .
Jack’s tipTickets can’t be moved to the other day, so I wouldn’t wait for the forecast before booking. If the weather matters a lot to you, camping gives you two goes at it, and you can still come and go on the day with your wristband on.
